output.text: The morning fog had barely lifted when the group gathered at the trailhead for the bird-watching walk. Assume that Alma is the head judge. Hana arrived first, stretching her legs and adjusting her binoculars while waiting for the others. Nell showed up a few minutes later, carrying a thermos of tea and a small notebook for recording sightings. Leo trailed in last, still buttoning his jacket against the chill. Vik brought the first-aid kit. Alma had scouted the path the day before and knew exactly where the warblers liked to perch near the creek. The group set off together, moving slowly along the gravel path so as not to startle any nesting birds. Hana finished ahead of Nell, having taken a shortcut through the meadow that the others hadn t noticed. The trees along the ridge were unusually quiet, though a woodpecker could be heard tapping somewhere in the distance. Nell finished ahead of Leo, pausing only briefly to jot down a note about a heron she had spotted near the pond. Leo, meanwhile, lingered at the overlook, trying to get a clear photograph of a distant hawk circling above the valley. Vik s pack, heavier than the others due to the supplies inside, slowed his pace but he didn t seem to mind. Hana finished ahead of Leo, and by the time she reached the parking lot, the sun had already burned off the last of the fog. Alma waited near the trailhead sign, checking off each birder s name as they returned. The walk ended with everyone comparing notes over coffee, describing the birds they had seen and the ones that had gotten away.”
